message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that depends on a handful of variables—crew size, weather, the number of coats required, and the logistics of working at extreme heights. In practice, the tower’s repaints have taken on the order of **six months to a year**.

### Why it takes that long

| Factor | How it affects the timeline |
|--------|-----------------------------|
| **Scale** | The tower is ~324 m tall and covers ~1.5 ha of iron. Even with a large crew, you can only work a few hundred square metres per day. |
| **Coats** | Each section typically receives 3–4 coats (primer, base, topcoat). Each coat must dry before the next is applied. |
| **Safety & Logistics** | Workers need harnesses, scaffolding, and transport to reach the upper levels. Setting up and dismantling equipment adds days. |
| **Weather** | Rain, wind, or extreme temperatures can halt work for hours or days. |
| **Inspection & Quality Control** | After each coat, inspectors check for coverage, adhesion, and surface defects. Re‑work can add weeks. |

### Rough Work‑Day Breakdown

| Stage | Typical Duration (days) | Notes |
|-------|------------------------|-------|
| **Preparation** (cleaning, priming) | 30–45 | Includes rust removal, sandblasting, and primer application. |
| **Base Coat** | 20–30 | Primer + first paint coat. |
| **Top Coat** | 20–30 | Final protective layer. |
| **Inspection & Touch‑ups** | 10–15 | Spot repairs, re‑priming if needed. |
| **Cleanup & Site Restoration** | 5–10 | Removing equipment, restoring access points. |

Assuming a crew of 50–70 workers operating 5 days a week, you’re looking at roughly **200–250 work‑days**—or **6–8 months** of continuous effort. If you add downtime for bad weather or supply delays, the project can stretch to **12 months**.

---

#### Bottom line

A full repaint of the Eiffel Tower would likely take **half a year to a year**, depending on crew size, weather, and the number of coats. That’s why the tower’s maintenance schedule is carefully planned and why the last major repaint (2011‑2012) spanned about two years of intermittent work.
